message.content: {"summary":"You submitted a strong, well-argued response: Q2 and Q4 are excellent, and Q3(a)(b) are correct. The main losses are the Q3(c) chain calculation, CAP misuse in Q5, a non-measurable availability measure in Q1, a one-sided ADR in Q6, and over-length answers affecting Q7. Total 30/40.","next_steps":["Recalculate Q3(c) using the full four-component chain availability, then convert the resulting downtime to hours per month and show the working.","Rewrite the Q5 CAP statement so partition tolerance is not treated as optional, make the Q1 availability response measure measurable, and add at least one negative consequence to Q6.","Trim Q1, Q2 and Q4 to 150 words or fewer, and check that required headings and IEEE citations remain correct."],"criteria":{"C1":"You justified performance and availability from the CampusEats scenario, and your performance scenario has all six parts with a measurable p95 target. The availability scenario is complete but its response measure, “stay up most of the time,” is not measurable. For Excellent, give both scenarios measurable response measures, such as a monthly uptime percentage or maximum downtime.","C2":"Your modular monolith recommendation is clear and well linked to the scenario. You used two specific trade-offs: five developers versus operational overhead, and the known single-VM/deployment problems not being caused by the monolith. You also acknowledged the downside that modules cannot scale independently and one bug can crash the process. This meets the Excellent level.","C3":"Parts (a) and (b) are correct with working shown: 99.30% and 5.0 hours. In part (c) you correctly combined payment availability but then applied only the payment-provider downtime, 0.018 hours, ignoring the other three components. The correct result is about 99.80% and 1.5 hours per month. For Excellent, all three parts must be correct.","C4":"Circuit Breaker is named and its Closed/Open/Half-Open mechanism is explained correctly. You applied it concretely to the 25-minute outage with a student-facing fallback message, and you gave a tuning consideration using a failure threshold and window. This meets the Excellent level.","C5":"Your choices are reasonable and you named concrete techniques: a Redis TTL cache and an idempotency key. However, your CAP statement says payments “give up partition tolerance,” which is incorrect: partition tolerance is not optional, and during a partition you must sacrifice consistency or availability. For Excellent, correct the CAP explanation while keeping both justified choices and techniques.","C6":"Context, Decision and Consequences are all present and specific to the CampusEats scenario. However, your consequences are entirely positive, citing improved response time and lunch-peak smoothing. For Excellent, add at least one negative consequence, such as eventual consistency, duplicate notifications, or added operational complexity.","C7":"Your writing is clear and IEEE-style references are provided. However, at least Q1 and Q2, and arguably Q4, exceed the 150-word limit, which is more than a single over-length answer. For Proficient, keep at most one answer over the limit and resolve minor citation or formatting problems."}}

We need to produce JSON formative feedback. Need address student as "you". Specific, supportive, actionable, cite sections/figures, name what did well, state next rubric level requires. Don't change marks. Don't comment on conversion artefacts. Don't make up explanations for unclear reasoning. Schema summary <=80 words, next_steps array of 3 strings, criteria object keyed by criterion id with <=70 words each.

Need include all criteria C1-C7. Summary <=80 words. Next steps 3 strings. Criteria feedback each <=70 words. Need mention marks? We can mention current level and next level. Don't change marks. Need be supportive. Need cite sections/figures. We have evidence quotes. Need not overdo. Need ensure each criterion feedback <=70 words. Summary <=80. Next steps maybe concise.

Need craft. C1: Proficient 4/6. You justified performance and availability from scenario; performance scenario six-part measurable; availability response measure "stay up most of the time" not measurable. Next Excellent requires both response measures measurable. Suggest quantify e.g. 99.9% monthly uptime or max downtime. C2 Excellent 6/6: modular monolith recommendation, trade-offs team size and known problems, downside acknowledged. Keep. C3 Proficient 5/8: (a)(b) correct with working; (c) combined payment availability but applied only payment downtime 0.018h, ignoring other components; correct ~99.80% and ~1.5h/month. Next Excellent requires all parts correct. C4 Excellent 5/5: circuit breaker mechanism, applied to outage, tuning threshold. C5 Proficient 4/6: choices reasonable and techniques Redis TTL/idempotency; CAP misstated "give up partition tolerance"; next Excellent requires correct CAP: partition tolerance not optional; during partition sacrifice C or A. C6 Proficient 4/5: context decision consequences present scenario-specific; consequences all positive; next Excellent requires at least one negative consequence e.g. eventual consistency/duplicate notifications/operational complexity. C7 Developing 2/4: writing clear and IEEE refs, but Q1 and Q2 (and arguably Q4) exceed 150 words; next Proficient requires at most one answer over limit and minor citation/format issues. Need maybe mention headings? Not in evidence. Don't make up. We can say "at least Q1 and Q2 exceed". Good.

The main losses are the Q3(c) chain calculation, CAP misuse in Q5, a non-measurable availability measure in Q1, a one-sided ADR in Q6, and over-length answers affecting Q7. Total 30/40." <=80 words. Count ~55. Good.

Next steps 3 strings: 1) Recalculate Q3(c) using full chain availability and convert downtime to monthly hours; show working. 2) Rewrite Q5 CAP sentence and Q1 availability response measure to be measurable; add negative consequence to Q6. 3) Trim Q1/Q2/Q4 to <=150 words and check headings/IEEE citations. Need actionable. Maybe combine. Ensure 3.

Need JSON only. No markdown. Use exact criterion ids. Each string <=70 words. Need avoid "figure" since no figures. Cite sections. Good.
